name: Cross-Chain App Workflow
goal: Build an application that operates across multiple chains — EVM (Base, Ethereum) and/or Solana — with a unified wallet experience, cross-chain asset visibility, and chain-specific RPC access.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When the app only needs to connect existing wallets across EVM chains — no embedded wallet creation needed. Reown (formerly WalletConnect) is the reference standard for connecting hardware wallets, MetaMask, and Ledger across EVM chains.
When the app targets new users who need an embedded wallet across multiple chains. Privy supports cross-chain embedded wallets but without the external wallet connection breadth of Dynamic.

phases.phase_notes: Dynamic is the correct choice for cross-chain apps because it is natively multi-chain — it supports EVM chains, Solana, Aptos, and more in a single SDK, handling both embedded wallet creation and external wallet connection (MetaMask, Phantom, Coinbase Wallet, Backpack) across chains. A cross-chain app that forces users to connect a different wallet for each chain will have catastrophic UX. Dynamic unifies the wallet context. Use Dynamic's network switcher to handle the EVM ↔ Solana transition cleanly.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When the app needs a single RPC provider for ALL chains including Solana, Polygon, Arbitrum, and others. QuickNode supports more chains than Alchemy in a single account. If chain breadth matters more than Base/Ethereum optimization, use QuickNode.

phases.phase_notes: For EVM chains (Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum), Alchemy provides the highest quality endpoints with enhanced APIs. If the cross-chain app includes Solana, a second RPC provider is needed for the Solana side — see the solana-rpc phase.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When already on QuickNode for EVM chains and want a single provider for all chains.

phases.phase_notes: Add this phase when the app includes Solana chain support. Helius provides Solana RPC + enhanced transaction parsing, DAS API for digital assets, and webhook support for Solana wallet activity. Required alongside alchemy-rpc if the app spans both EVM and Solana.

scale_overrides.mvp: Skip if EVM-only in MVP. Add Solana support as a follow-on phase — do not attempt full cross-chain from day one if not strictly required.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When the app only needs EVM token prices and does not require Solana-specific portfolio data. CoinGecko has broader token coverage but no Solana portfolio analytics.

phases.phase_notes: For cross-chain portfolio apps, Birdeye provides unified token price and portfolio data across Solana and EVM chains — a single API that aggregates DEX prices from both ecosystems. Required for any app that shows 'your total portfolio value' across chains.

scale_overrides.hackathon: Skip unless portfolio display is the core demo feature.

alternative_tools.when_to_prefer: When session keys or advanced smart account programmability across EVM chains is needed, beyond standard gas sponsorship.

phases.phase_notes: Gas sponsorship applies to EVM chains only — Solana has native priority fee mechanics handled separately. If the app sponsors gas on Base/Ethereum but uses Solana natively, Pimlico covers EVM and Jito (from the solana-consumer-app workflow) covers Solana priority fees. Note: cross-chain gas sponsorship requires separate configurations per chain.

scale_overrides.mvp: Optional. Add when the EVM-side user flows require transactions and user-facing gas fees degrade UX.

production_notes: Cross-chain UX is hard. The single biggest UX failure in cross-chain apps is forcing users to think about which chain they are on. Dynamic's network abstraction helps, but the app must handle chain-switching errors, wrong-network states, and pending transactions across chains gracefully.

Chain-specific features are real: Solana accounts have rent, EVM accounts have nonce, Solana transactions expire after ~90 seconds, EVM transactions can be replaced. Build chain-specific error handling, not a generic error handler.
Two RPC provider relationships (Alchemy + Helius) means two API keys, two rate limits, and two billing relationships. Build monitoring for both from day one.

Bridging assets across chains is explicitly out of scope for this workflow — bridging requires integrating a cross-chain bridge protocol (LayerZero, Wormhole, Across). If bridging is required, it is a separate feature with significant security surface area.

Token addresses are chain-specific — the same token (e.g., USDC) has different contract addresses on Base, Ethereum, and Solana. Build a token registry abstraction that maps symbol → chain → address to avoid hardcoded address errors.
tradeoffs: Dynamic's multi-chain support is excellent for wallet management but adds SDK complexity compared to a chain-specific library. The UX improvement from unified wallet context is worth the setup overhead.
Two RPC providers (Alchemy + Helius) is more complex than one but provides optimal quality per chain. QuickNode as a single provider trades per-chain optimization for operational simplicity.

Building cross-chain from day one vs. expanding later: expanding chain support later is significantly harder than building multi-chain architecture from the start. If Solana is on the product roadmap, include Dynamic (not a Solana-incompatible EVM-only wallet SDK) from day one.

Birdeye for cross-chain portfolio data is opinionated — Solana price data is excellent, EVM data is good but not as comprehensive as Alchemy's token API. Multi-chain portfolio apps may need to reconcile data from multiple sources.
anti_patterns: Using a chain-specific wallet SDK (wagmi-only, Solana-wallet-adapter-only) for a cross-chain app — forces separate wallet connections per chain, which is an UX anti-pattern.

Treating cross-chain as 'just add another RPC endpoint' — chain-specific semantics (account model, transaction lifecycle, fee model, finality guarantees) require chain-specific handling throughout the stack.
Building bridge functionality in-house — cross-chain bridging is a security-critical primitive. Use established bridge protocols (LayerZero, Wormhole) or exclude bridging from scope.
Hardcoding token addresses without a chain-registry abstraction — the same token has different addresses on each chain. A hardcoded address that works on Ethereum will be wrong on Base or Solana.
Not handling chain-switching UX — users on the wrong chain should get a clear 'switch to X' prompt, not a cryptic transaction failure.

constraint_modifiers.modification: Remove the solana-rpc phase. Use Alchemy + wagmi for EVM-only cross-chain (Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum). Replace Dynamic with Reown if no embedded wallet creation is needed.
Use Reown for external wallet connection across EVM chains. Use Dynamic if Solana wallet support is also needed.
Pick one chain for the MVP and build chain-specific. Add cross-chain support in a follow-on. A hackathon cross-chain implementation is almost always a single-chain demo with cross-chain branding.
Add Vercel AI SDK for portfolio analysis, trade recommendations, or cross-chain data interpretation. Pass aggregated Birdeye + Alchemy token data as context to the LLM.

source.derived_from: corpus-expansion — CEO review gap analysis. Cross-chain app pattern validated against multi-chain production apps.
